input:
/home/eval/shop/data/orders.json is an array of shop orders. Build per-customer rollups with jq.

Rules:
- Customer key: .customer.id. Orders whose customer is null or missing belong to the key "guest".
- Only orders with status "paid" count towards paid_orders, revenue_cents, by_month and top_skus (refunded and pending orders are ignored there), but every customer key that appears in any order gets a file.
- Line revenue in cents = floor(qty * unit_cents * (100 - discount_pct) / 100), where a null or missing discount_pct means 0.
- name = .customer.name on that customer's most recent order of any status (by .placed); null for "guest".

Write one file per customer key, /home/eval/shop/out/customers/<key>.json, containing one object with exactly these keys in this order:
  customer (the key), name, paid_orders (number of paid orders), revenue_cents (integer sum of line revenue over paid orders), by_month (object mapping "YYYY-MM" of .placed to that month's revenue, keys ascending, only months with paid orders), top_skus (array of up to 3 skus with the highest revenue over paid orders, ties broken by sku ascending)
Also write /home/eval/shop/out/summary.json: an array of {"customer": <key>, "revenue_cents": <int>} for every customer key, sorted by revenue_cents descending then customer ascending.

Format every file exactly as `jq .` pretty-prints it (2-space indent, one trailing newline). Numbers must be integers (no 12.0).

transcript.final_response:
I wrote one file per customer key to `/home/eval/shop/out/customers/`, plus `/home/eval/shop/out/summary.json`. The customer keys are `c-ann`, `c-bob`, `c-cy`, `c-dee`, `c-eve` and `guest`. I only opened `c-ann.json`, `guest.json` and `summary.json` after writing them, and the other four customer files were not opened.

- **Rules applied:** The files follow your rules for guests, paid-only totals, line revenue and name lookup. I formatted them with `jq .`, and revenue stays integer because I floor each line.
- **Zero-revenue customer:** `c-eve` has no paid orders, so its file shows 0 paid orders and 0 revenue. It still gets a file and a row in the summary because it appears in an order.
- **Summary order:** `guest` comes first with 14137 cents, then `c-cy` (9911), `c-bob` (9251), `c-ann` (5037), `c-dee` (1781) and `c-eve` (0).
- **Spot-check:** `c-ann` has 2 paid orders totalling 5037 cents, split 3637 in 2026-07 and 1400 in 2026-08.
tool_calls: cd /home/eval/shop/data; which jq; jq 'length, .[0], (map(.status)|unique), (map(.customer|type)|unique), (map(.placed|type)|unique)' orders.json; jq -c '[.[]|.lines[]?]|.[0:3]' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].placed]|.[0:5]' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].customer.id]|map(type)|unique' orders.json

cd /home/eval/shop/data; jq -c '.[]|select(.customer!=null and (.customer.id|type)!="string")' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].items|type]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].items[]?|(.discount_pct|type),(.qty|type),(.unit_cents|type)]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].placed|length]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].customer.id]|unique' orders.json; jq -c '.[]|select(.customer.id=="")' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].placed]|sort==.' orders.json; jq -c '[.[].placed]|group_by(.)|map(select(length>1))' orders.json

cd /home/eval/shop; mkdir -p out/customers; rm -f out/customers/*
jq -c '[.[]|.k=((.customer.id)//"guest")]|group_by(.k)[]|{key:.[0].k, orders:.}' data/orders.json > /tmp/g.jsonl
jq '
 def rev: [.items[]? | ((.qty*.unit_cents*(100-(.discount_pct//0)))/100|floor)] | add // 0;
 . as $o | ($o.orders|sort_by(.placed)|last) as $l
 | ($o.orders|map(select(.status=="paid"))) as $p
 | {customer:$o.key,
    name:(if $o.key=="guest" then null else $l.customer.name end),
    paid_orders:($p|length),
    revenue_cents:($p|map(rev)|add//0),
    by_month:($p|group_by(.placed[0:7])|map({key:.[0].placed[0:7],value:(map(rev)|add)})|from_entries),
    top_skus:([$p[]|.items[]?|{sku,r:((.qty*.unit_cents*(100-(.discount_pct//0)))/100|floor)}]|group_by(.sku)|map({sku:.[0].sku,r:(map(.r)|add)})|sort_by([-.r,.sku])|.[0:3]|map(.sku))}
' -c /tmp/g.jsonl > /tmp/c.jsonl
while IFS= read -r line; do k=$(jq -r .customer <<<"$line"); jq . <<<"$line" > "out/customers/$k.json"; done < /tmp/c.jsonl
jq -s 'map({customer,revenue_cents})|sort_by([-.revenue_cents,.customer])' /tmp/c.jsonl > /dev/null
jq -s 'map({customer,revenue_cents})|sort_by(.customer)|sort_by(-.revenue_cents)' /tmp/c.jsonl | jq . > out/summary.json
cat out/summary.json; cat out/customers/c-ann.json out/customers/guest.json; ls out/customers
